title: An assembler for the tiny computer

milestone.title: From Machine Code to Modern Languages

description:
Write the assembler from lesson 5.01: it reads a program in the tiny computer's assembly language and prints the numbers to put in memory - the input the computer you built in the milestone 4 project runs.

```
        LOAD  counter      ; the countdown from 4.04
top:    JUMPZ done
        SUB   one
        STORE counter
        JUMP  top
done:   HALT
counter: 3
one:     1
```

prints

```
106 605 307 406 501 0 3 1
```

The language, one item per line:
- `; ...` is a comment, and blank lines are skipped.
- A line may start with a **label**: a name followed by `:`.
- Then an **instruction** (`LOAD`, `ADD`, `SUB`, `STORE`, `JUMP`, `JUMPZ` with one operand, or `HALT` with none; any case), or a plain **number** (data for that cell), or nothing (a label alone names the next cell).
- An operand is a number or a label defined anywhere in the program (also further down).
- Every instruction and every number takes the next memory cell, starting at 0.

Read lines until the end of the input. Print the cells on one line, separated by spaces. On the first error, print only the error and stop:

| Problem | Message |
|---|---|
| An unknown instruction name | `Line N: unknown instruction NAME` |
| An operand that is neither a number nor a known label | `Line N: unknown label NAME` |
| A label defined twice | `Line N: label NAME is already defined` |
| More than 16 cells | `The program needs N cells, but there are only 16` |

Line numbers count from 1 and include blank lines and comments.
hints: Pass one only counts: a line with something after its label takes one cell. Pass two can then look any label up in the dictionary.
requirements: Work in **two passes**: the first finds every label's cell number, the second turns each line into a number. (A label can be used before the line that defines it, so one pass is not enough.)
Write a function that assembles a single instruction.

examples.name: the countdown
examples.stdin:
LOAD  counter      ; the countdown from 4.04
top:    JUMPZ done
        SUB   one
        STORE counter
        JUMP  top
done:   HALT
counter: 3
one:     1

examples.name: multiply, lower case and comments
examples.stdin:
; multiply 4 by 3 by adding
loop:   load left
        jumpz finish
        sub one
        store left
        load total
        add number
        store total
        jump loop
finish: halt

number: 4
left:   3
total:  0
one:    1
